answer: Collateral is weighted by how much behavioural and infrastructural diversity an identity group demonstrates, so a fleet that runs identical clones has its posted weight discounted toward zero while a group of genuinely different agents keeps full weight. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Read it as a relic weighed by haven against every dawn nearby: identical dawn groups cancel the haven and strip the relic of value, while a dawn with its own history keeps both. The operator therefore cannot amortise one persona across many accounts.
